evidence_spans: To quantify the accompanying radiation suppression, we fit the simulated inverse Q factor to a sixth-order momentum expansion of 1 2 4 6 1 1 1x x xQ k k k  − = + + with the extracted coefficients shown in Fig. 3(c). At f = 0.35, near the BIC-merging transition, the quadratic coefficient nearly vanishes with α1 = 4×10-7, while the quartic coefficient becomes small and negative (β1 = -1.7×10-3), reflecting competing higher-order radiation contributions.

We validate the predicted band selection and BIC-merging mechanism using finite-element simulations of a rectangular PCS with lattice periods ax = 270 nm and ay = 300 nm, thickness h = 150 nm and refractive index nslab = 2.6.
CLM-PHOT-0176.statement: The finite-element simulation of the rectangular PCS with f = 0.35 yields a fitted quadratic expansion coefficient α1 = 4 × 10^-7 for the inverse Q factor.
